A growing challenge in modern COMPUTING science is the need for teams to reason across models, data, and domain knowledge that span multiple disciplines. The knowledge of human team members rarely spans this breadth and depth, and information overload is amplified as new data, models, and findings proliferate. NLR is researching how to address this challenge by enhancing the effectiveness of AI scientific assistants as laboratory teammates and improving the scientific capabilities of the large language models that power these assistants today. Areas of focus include uncertainty management, probabilistic reasoning, and multimodal data analysis. Extreme-scale computing and AI-model-powered reasoning frameworks are critical enablers for this effort. Theseus leverages GPU nodes on Kestrel for fine-tuning and inference of AI models and agents. An early case study focuses on turbulence modeling—an important element of energy systems research.
